qs.q: A patient with chronic heart failure is started on digoxin. Which pharmacodynamic effect is primarily responsible for its therapeutic benefit?
qs.e: Digoxin inhibits Na+/K+ ATPase, increasing intracellular calcium and enhancing myocardial contractility.
qs.s: Weekly Pharmacology Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with chronic pain is prescribed tramadol. Which pharmacodynamic mechanism contributes to its analgesic effect?
qs.e: Tramadol acts as an opioid agonist and inhibits serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake.
qs.s: Weekly Pharmacology Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with hypertension is started on losartan. Which pharmacodynamic effect is primarily responsible for its antihypertensive action?
qs.e: Losartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker that inhibits the effects of angiotensin II.
qs.s: Weekly Pharmacology Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with diabetes is prescribed metformin. Which pharmacodynamic mechanism is primarily responsible for its glucose-lowering effect?
qs.e: Metformin decreases hepatic glucose production and increases peripheral insulin sensitivity.
qs.s: Weekly Pharmacology Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with asthma is prescribed salbutamol. Which pharmacodynamic mechanism is responsible for its bronchodilator effect?
qs.e: Salbutamol is a beta-2 agonist that stimulates beta-2 adrenergic receptors in bronchial smooth muscle.
qs.s: Weekly Pharmacology Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with depression is prescribed fluoxetine. Which pharmacodynamic mechanism is primarily responsible for its antidepressant effect?
o: Prevents serotonin reabsorption at neuronal synaptic clefts.
Reduces activity of the monoamine oxidase enzyme.
Blocks dopamine receptors located in the central nervous system.
Decreases norepinephrine reuptake at synaptic junctions.
Enhances activation of GABA‑A receptor channels.
qs.e: Fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor that increases synaptic serotonin levels.
qs.s: Weekly Pharmacology Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with hyperlipidemia is prescribed atorvastatin. Which pharmacodynamic mechanism is responsible for its lipid-lowering effect?
o: Lowers intestinal cholesterol absorption from the gut.
Diminishes activity of the lipoprotein lipase enzyme.
Blocks the HMG‑CoA reductase enzyme responsible for cholesterol synthesis.
Prevents bile‑acid reabsorption within the intestinal lumen.
qs.e: Atorvastatin inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol synthesis.
qs.s: Weekly Pharmacology Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with gout is prescribed allopurinol. Which pharmacodynamic mechanism is responsible for its uric acid-lowering effect?
o: Decreases renal reabsorption of uric acid.
Inhibits the activity of the xanthine oxidase enzyme.
Suppresses the synthesis of purine nucleotides.
Lowers hepatic production of uric acid.
qs.e: Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, reducing the conversion of hypoxanthine to uric acid.
qs.s: Weekly Pharmacology Exam - November 6, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)
